decisions.title: Two years old, and a new toy
decisions.body: Abdramane can walk quite well now. With a new toy in hand, what does the child do first? What you pick leans the child's temperament that way; moments like these add up, and it settles by about age five.
decisions.fact: Temperament comes from what we are born with and what happens as we grow. Twin studies put about 40% of the differences

t: In January undefined, you were born a boy in rural Maradi Region, Niger, into a family in the bottom 20–40%. You have 10 older siblings. Your family's religion is Islam.
You got your basic vaccinations (DTP and measles).
You took your first steps. The whole family clapped.
You tried again and again, and at last you did it by yourself.
You played in the mud and got your clothes filthy.
Your paternal grandmother slipped you some pocket money on the quiet. (+$3)
At home, meals were cooked over a smoky fire. When smoke filled the kitchen, your eyes stung and you coughed.
In the rainy season the lanes swelled like rivers. You and the neighbourhood children sailed paper boats on the muddy water.
Every morning you learned to read the Quran at the neighbourhood mosque.
You and Kadidiatou became best friends.
You fell in love with drawing and painting.
You spent your days tending the small plot that came with the house.
You spent Eid al-Fitr (the feast after Ramadan) with your family.
Your older sister married and left home.
Your older sister married and left home.
You waited in a long line at the well to fill the water jug.
You envied your friends who went to school.
Before sunrise you carried a water can to the far well and back. The way home always felt longer.
You stayed with your family instead of going to school.
New clothes came only once a year, for the holidays.
Your older sister married and left home.
You went online for the first time. Your world got bigger.
There was no electricity, so after sunset you lived by lamplight.
With a ball made of rolled-up plastic bags, you played football barefoot until the sun went down.
Your older sister married and left home.
You and Haoua became best friends.
You gave your pictures to family and friends.
You handed it in at the police post. A few days later you heard the owner had collected it.
You were sick with the flu for a week.
Days of thick blowing dust went on, and you could not play outside.
Your voice began to crack and deepen. You shot up in a year, and your trousers were soon too short.
You spent Eid al-Fitr (the feast after Ramadan) with your family.
You went to a friend's wedding and helped with the cooking.
You started working as a smallholder farmer.
Every morning you walked a long way to fetch water.
You got a second-hand smartphone you could afford.
There was no electricity, so after sunset you lived by lamplight.
The harvest was good this year.
You and Zénabou became best friends.
Walking home after selling your harvest at the market, your steps felt light.
You walked the neighborhood until the neighbors' runaway puppy was found.
You had a crush on a friend from the neighborhood.
All your brothers and sisters gathered at home.
A few years after marrying, your older brother moved out to a home of their own.
You and Bakary became best friends.
The harvest was good this year.
You started dating Fatoumata.
You contributed toward a relative's funeral. (−$6)
You raised a toast at an old friend's wedding. (−$8)
You spent Eid al-Fitr (the feast after Ramadan) with your family.
You got married!
After the wedding you went on living with your mother under one roof.
The kitchen, where meals were cooked over a fire, was always thick with smoke.
Your pictures hung on the wall of a local cafe. Someone even asked to buy one.
Whenever friends talked about having a crush, you found you did not really feel that pull. Learning that some people are like that was a relief.
At a friend's wedding you danced and celebrated late into the night.
The two of you decided to live without children.
You changed jobs and now work as a fisher.
After many trips to the court and the offices, your birth was registered late and you got an identity card. (−$35)
You got together with old friends and talked all night.
You took your mother, who lives with you, back and forth to the hospital. (−$28)
You spent Eid al-Fitr (the feast after Ramadan) with your family.
A bad cold kept you in bed for several days.
A sibling had a baby. You held your niece or nephew for the first time.
The medicine and hospital bills for your mother, who lives with you, went up. (−$33)
On the boat heading home with a full catch, everyone sang together.
You took Ngoné as your second wife. The wedding and the gifts to the bride's family cost $468. Things were cold between you and Fatoumata for a while.
You had a big fight with a sibling and made up a few months later.
You took your mother, who lives with you, back and forth to the hospital. (−$34)
Your second wife Ngoné gave birth to a son, Lassina Cissé.
Mending nets, you swapped stories of the sea with the fishermen from the next boat.
Lassina called you 'Dad' for the first time.
